title: Garmin Sales Begin: Huge deals on Garmin Fenix, Edge, Forerunner Series and more!
content:
Like clockwork, Garmin has put forth their sale plans for the Black Friday and Holiday season. Garmin is actually one of the most predictable companies in this space when it comes to sales and how they structure them (with Wahoo probably being *the* most predictable one). The sale prices Garmin puts forth now are essentially their deals for the holidays. They don’t tend to reduce prices on these specific products further, and don’t really add anything else. This is it, at least from a US perspective (European sales are the Wild West and field of dreams of pricing…anything is possible).

The exception to that rule in the US is Uncle Amazon. Uncle Amazon has a long history of throwing very random deals into the mix, especially over Black Friday weekend. These tend to fall into one of two buckets. The first is buckets where Garmin has basically worked with Amazon to offload huge chunks of older inventory, and you’ll see some crazy deals on that. The second is when Amazon doesn’t partner with Garmin at all, and simply decides to randomly cut the price yolo style. This is usually previous-generation stuff, but at least once or twice over each Black Friday it ends up being a newly released product.

Anyway, my advice here is simple: If you see something on sale you want, buy it now, and then if you find a better Amazon deal later, you can always return it or such. For Amazon, you can return items bought Nov 1-Dec 31st until Jan 31st 2027. As always, the random deals don’t tend to last. They’re flash in the pans. Got that?

With that, onto the deals! And thanks for supporting the site via the links below. As an Amazon Associate, I earn from qualifying purchases. Enjoy!

Watches & Wearables:

This covers anything you can wear that’s watch-like or activity band-like, including sensors.

ProductSale PriceAmazonOther siteSale Notes
Garmin Bounce 2 Kids Smartwatch with LTE - $50 off!$249AmazonREIThis is Garmin's kids-focused and LTE connected smart watch. Our three daughters have been using it for the last year, after using the original Bounce 1 for many years. This is a *massive* upgrade over the Bounce 1, both in features/hardware, but frankly also battery life.
Garmin Enduro 3 - $100 off!
$899		$699AmazonWhile the Garmin Enduro 4 just came out ($899), it was basically just a new case, more storage, and slightly faster map rendering. The rest of the new software features still go back to the Enduro 3, which is great!
Garmin Fenix 8 Pro Series - $250 off!$849AmazonREIIf you were looking for the Fenix 9 but didn't quite want to spend the money, the Fenix 8 Pro is getting virtually every software feature through a set of firmware updates. Remember all Fenix 8 Pro has LTE inReach, versus only the Fenix 9 Pro inReach models have LTE inREach (meaning, don't just compare the base Fenix 9 price, since it doesn't have the LTE inReach features/hardware).
Garmin Fenix 8 Series - $275 Off!
$999-$1,199		$725AmazonREI⚡ This is now the lowest price the Fenix 8 has been at. And while the Fenix 9 was just a few months ago, Garmin has announced a major shift in that the Fenix 8 will get virtually all the new Fenix 9 software features. That's a massive update. If deciding between Fenix 8 and Fenix 8 Pro, the TLDR there is if you care about LTE inReach, go Fenix 8 Pro, if not, probably just save the cash and go Fenix 8.
Garmin Forerunner 170 - $35 off!
$299/$349 (with Music)		$314AmazonLike the Forerunner 70 sale, this isn't an official deal - just Amazon doing Amazon. If you want it, grab it before someone changes their mind or gets upset.
Garmin Forerunner 570 - $100 off!
$549		$449AmazonREII'm not a huge fan of this watch, not because it's bad, but because it lacks the maps that every other watch on the market at $450-$600 has. Garmin also made some weird choices on non-mapping features they didn't include from the FR970. Still, there's a *ton* of people that don't care about maps, and are very happy with this watch. And arguebly, if I didn't care about maps, I'd be happy with this watch in a Garmin ecosystem.
Garmin Forerunner 70 - $20 off
$249		$230AmazonThis one is an official sale, one of the Uncle Amazon ones if you will. It's not a massive discount, and it seems to vary by the hour. But hey, if you were in the market for this unit... go forth!
Garmin Forerunner 970 - $100 off!
$749		$649AmazonREI⚡ The Garmin FR970 is Garmin's top-end Forerunner watch, which is a full multi-sport watch. It nearly all the same features as a Fenix 9 does software-wise, except simply lacks the exterior design (or the LTE inReach features). If you want a lighter weight Fenix, this is it.
Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED - $200 off!
$399/$449/$499		$249AmazonREIThis is now (by far) the lowest price we've seen the Instinct 3 series at, and in particular the Instinct 3 AMOLED.
Garmin Instinct 3 SOLAR - $100 off$249AmazonREIThis is also the lowest price we've seen the Instinct 3 SOLAR at before, the previous low watermark was $300.
Garmin Venu 4 - $10 off!$449AmazonREIThis is actually the lowest price the Venu 4 has been thus far. It's Garmin's most direct competitor to an Apple Watch, Pixel Watch, Samsung Watch, in terms of being mainstream. It has medical grade ECG, plus all the other sports features you expect.
Garmin Venu X1 - $200 off!$499AmazonREI⚡ This is now the lowest price we've ever seen the Venu X1. This is basically a blend of a Forerunner 970, Venu 4, and Fenix 8...but super thin. For whatever reason, this simply hasn't sold well, despite actually being one of the best deals out there in sports tech.
Garmin Vivoactive 6 - $50 off!
$299		$249AmazonREIThe Vivoactive 6 is essentially a Venu 4, but without the voice/calling/ECG features (and a few other tidbits). It's probably one of the best deals in Garmin's lineup (sale or otherwise), though the introduction of the Forerunner 70 at the $249 price point might be a better deal (and ~$230 right now on sale).

Cycling Gear & Trainers:

Got a bike? Then this section is for you.

ProductSale PriceAmazonOther siteSale Notes
Garmin Edge 1050 - $100 off!$599AmazonREIWhile Garmin just announced the Edge 1060 a few weeks ago, the Edge 1050 is getting the majority of the new software features (many are already out in beta!). Setting aside the 1060, it's easily the next best/most capable bike computer on the market, especially if you like a larger display.
Garmin Edge 550 - $100 off!$399AmazonREIFun fact: I've actually used this as my main bike GPS all the way till the Edge 1060 released a few weeks ago. Despite not having a touchscreen, I've gotten used to that aspect. I prefer the 850's touchscreen, but am also perfectly happy with this too. Like the Edge 850, it also gets most of the new 1060 software updates as well.
Garmin Edge 850 - $100 off!$499AmazonREIThis is Garmin's newest mid-size bike computer. They've got the bigger sized 1050/1060 (larger display), and the Edge 850 is confirmed to get almost all the features from the newly announced 1060 a few weeks ago.
Garmin Rally RK210 (Dual Look KEO Power Meter Pedals) - $200 off!$799AmazonREI
Garmin Rally RS210 (Dual SPD-SL Power Meter Pedals) - $200 off$799AmazonREI
Garmin Rally XC210 (Dual SPD Power Meter Pedals) - $200 off$799Amazon
Garmin Varia Radar (RTL515) - $50 off
$199		$149AmazonREILook at fruitcake at the holdiays, no Garmin sale is complete without this thing being at $149. While it has micro-USB, it's still more or less the gold standard radar outside of Garmin's newer Varia Vue 820 (also on sale). This is Garmin's standalone radar/taillight option. This product is universally loved, and works with Garmin/Wahoo/Stages/Hammerhead/etc, and other bike computers.
Garmin Varia RearView 820 Cycling Radar - $50 off!$249AmazonREI⚡ This is Garmin's newest Varia radar (with USB-C!), that is easily the most accurate and feature-rich radar out there today. On one hand, some of the features are overkill, on the other end, it does work well. Garmin has quietly toned down some of the most annoying things over the past 10 months (such as a new low-threat mode toggle). It's what both myself and my wife use on the regular.
Garmin Varia Vue Front Light/Camera - $150 off!$399AmazonREIThis is the lowest price we've seen to date here for this combintion camera + light unit. It's not my favorite Garmin product, but equally there's really only two choices in the market for this device type (the other being Cycliq). They both have their pros and cons, to say the least. But, both do a good job at their core function of capturing footage in an accident.
ProductSale PriceAmazonOther siteSale Notes
Tacx Alpine Gradient Simulator - $100 off$999AmazonThis can pair up to most recent Tacx trainers to lift the front up/down of your bike, simulating the gradient.
Tacx Flux 2 Smart Trainer - $200 ish off
$899		$499N/AREIDear god, please don't buy this. Really, I don't see why anyone would buy this trainer at any price above $249. With the JetBlack Victory at $399 being more accurate, quiter, including WiFi, including Zwift Cog support (or mechanical cassette), including dual-Bluetooth, including Race Mode, and...one could go on and on. And the same goes for the KICKR CORE 2 that floats in the $400's on sale.

Other Sports & Fitness:

This is the catch-all bucket.

ProductSale PriceAmazonOther siteSale Notes
Garmin inReach 2 Mini Satellite Communicator (2-way) - $150 off$249AmazonREI⚡ This is a steal of a price for this. For years this had been my defacto satellite communicator when out of coverage area (till the Mini 3 Plus came out), using it on countless major treks outside of cellular service, both in a 24x7 tracking mode for friends and family, but also there in case of emergency. Would strongly recommend for anyone doing anything in the wilderness.
Garmin inReach Messenger - $100 off$199AmazonREIThis is essentially the lowest entry point into Garmin's inReach satellite messaging/tracking platform. This form factor is more ideal when placed on a surface (e.g. on the dashboard of a vehicle), than the inReach Mini which hanges from a backpack/straps/etc... Functionally speaking at their core, they all have basically the same features when used with the app. It's extra hardware bits like supporting voice/photo messages that differentiate it the most.
Garmin inReach Messenger Plus - $100 off!$299AmazonREIThe key difference with the new Plus model is that it adds the ability to send photos and voice messenges via satellite. I've used it a bit, and it's pretty cool because it makes it a lot faster to just say something rather than type it out.
Garmin inReach Mini 3 - $100 off$349AmazonREILook, just either get the inReach Mini 2 at $249 on sale right now, or spend $50 more and get the much more capable inReach Mini 3 Plus for $399. The Mini 3 is a weird mostly re-badged Mini 2, without all the best features of the Mini 3 Plus. Ok?
Garmin inReach Mini 3 Plus(Satellite Messenger) - $100 off!$399AmazonREIThis is my go to inReach device, and this is the biggest discount we've seen thus far. The key difference with this new Plus model is that it adds the ability to send photos and voice messenges via satellite, which can be handy for explaning something complicated without a bunch of typing. The main advantage over a phone/watch is that this also can share a long-term track of your progress and planned route to friends/family.

Europe Folks Note: I’ve tried in the past to keep track of all the separate Amazon European sites, and honestly, I have given up. With 100+ products on the US list, and then cross-checking each one manually across each country…has proven impossible. That said, you can click any link and, in theory (strong hopefully theory), it’s often also on sale in the EU sites.
author: DC Rainmaker
